definitions.text: Elements present in a group of the periodic table show similar chemical properties owning to the presence of same number of electrons in their outermost shells. However, a small variation in the chemical properties of elements is expected because the atomic size increases down the group.
All the elements present in group 1 have ns¹ configuration in their outermost shells. They are also called alkali metals.
These elements are thus named as Halogens which means salt-forming elements.
Oxidation is a process in which an electron is lost. The substance which loses an electron is called a reducing agent.
On the contrary, reduction is a process in which an electron is gained and the substance which accepts the electron is called an oxidizing agent.
Oxidation-reduction are simultaneous reactions. In other words an, electron is lost only when there is a substance to accept it.
Elements present at the centre of the modern periodic table from group 3 to group 12 are called d block elements or transition elements.
Elements present in group 18 of the modern periodic table are called noble elements.
Metals are defined as the elements which can generally form cations easily. They also tend to form metallic bond.
Metals can be hammered into thin sheets. This property is called malleability.
Metals can also be drawn into wires and this property is named as ductility.
Atomic size increases from top to bottom for elements of group-1. It becomes easier for these elements to lose their single electron.
Chemical reactivity of the elements in group-1 increases down the group.
Due to increase in their atomic sizes, the interatomic attraction decrease down the first group elements. This makes them softer and their melting points decrease down the group.
Due to increase in the size and volume of atoms, the densities of alkali metals increases down the group.
Group 17 elements or halogens exist as diatomic molecules. They are very reactive non-metals and react with alkali and alkaline earth metals.
Halogens are oxidising agents and their oxidising power decreases down the group.
In hydrogen halides the bond between hydrogen and halogen gets weaker as we go down the group. Hence, the thermal stability of hydrogen halides decreases down the group.
d – block elements or transition elements are all metals. They are often hard and have higher densities. These elements and their compounds are used as catalysts in important industrial reactions.
Noble gases are all unreactive gases because their outermost shells are complete.

fullMarks: For a trend question, state the direction first (up or down the group), then link it to atomic size and the resulting ease of losing or accepting electrons.
When comparing alkali metals reacting with chlorine, write the balanced equations and describe the reaction strength in order: lithium, steady; sodium, vigorous; potassium, violent.
For displacement and redox questions, identify which species is oxidized and which is reduced; chlorine displaces bromide or iodide because its oxidizing power is greater.
For hydrogen-halide stability, explain the chain clearly: halogen size increases down the group, the H–halogen bond gets weaker, less heat is needed to break it, and thermal stability decreases.

For a catalyst question, name the catalyst, the process and the change it helps bring about; for a catalytic converter, state that harmful exhaust gases are converted to less harmful gases and name platinum, palladium and rhodium.

For comparisons of metals and non-metals, cover conductivity, malleability and ductility, strength, and melting/boiling points; include graphite as an exception for electrical conduction and mercury as an exception for metals being solid.
For any calculation, write the given data in SI units, state the formula, substitute values with units, and give the final answer with its unit and appropriate significant figures.
mistakes: Mistake: Saying alkali metals become less reactive down the group. Fix: Their atomic size increases, so their outer electron is lost more easily and reactivity increases.
Mistake: Reversing the halogen trend and claiming reactivity increases down the group. Fix: Larger atoms attract an incoming electron less strongly, so halogen reactivity decreases down the group.
Mistake: Calling sodium the reducing agent in the chlorine–sodium bromide equation. Fix: Bromide ions lose electrons to form bromine, so bromide is oxidized and acts as the reducing agent.
Mistake: Saying iodine is solid only because it is a large atom. Fix: Explain that larger halogen molecules attract one another more strongly, raising melting and boiling points.
Mistake: Saying HBr is more thermally stable than HCl because bromine is below chlorine. Fix: The H–Br bond is weaker, so it takes less heat to break than the H–Cl bond.

Mistake: Naming only one metal in a catalytic converter or saying it removes all exhaust gases. Fix: Name platinum, palladium and rhodium, and state that the device converts more harmful gases into gases that do not pollute the atmosphere.
Mistake: Giving an unbalanced reaction or omitting physical state symbols when reproducing an equation. Fix: Check atom counts on both sides and copy the equation with its printed state symbols.

shortTheory.question: Why does it become easier to cut an alkali metal when we move from top to bottom in a group?
shortTheory.answer: Increase in the atomic size down the first group also weakens the interatomic attraction of the atomic metals. This fact makes them softer down the group and their melting points decrease.

shortTheory.question: Predict the reactivity of potassium towards halogens.
shortTheory.answer: Halogens are very reactive non-metals and react with alkali and alkaline earth metals. The chemical reactivity of the elements in group-1 increases down the group. Therefore, potassium reacts vigorously with halogens to form potassium halides.

shortTheory.question: Which noble gas should have the lowest boiling point and why?
shortTheory.answer: Helium should have the lowest boiling point because noble gases have very low boiling points and helium is the smallest noble gas.

shortTheory.question: Why does iodine exist in the solid state at room temperature?
shortTheory.answer: Atomic radii, melting and boiling points of halogens increase when you go down the group. This is because the atoms get larger as they have more electrons. As a result the molecules which are formed from these atoms will attract each other with a stronger force.

shortTheory.question: Why are transition elements different from normal elements?
shortTheory.answer: Transition elements are often hard with higher densities. Their melting and boiling points are also high. These metals show variable oxidation states and the compounds they form are often coloured. They are malleable and ductile.

shortTheory.question: Explain the role of catalytic converter in an automobile.
shortTheory.answer: A catalytic converter is a device used in the exhaust of an automobile which converts more harmful gases produced in the engine to such gases which do not pollute the atmosphere. Platinum, palladium and rhodium are the catalysts used in catalytic converters.
